title: Fleet insurance: vehicle inventory, policies and renewal
excerpt: Organise fleet insurance in Moldova: vehicle lists, RCA, CASCO, routes, documents and renewals, with a clear basis for comparing proposals.

seo.description: Prepare a company vehicle inventory, separate RCA and CASCO policies, check routes and renewal dates, then compare the same fleet and conditions.
seo.keywords: fleet insurance Moldova, company vehicle inventory, RCA CASCO renewal, fleet policies, vehicle insurance documents

content:
Fleet insurance begins with accurate vehicle and policy records, not the same package for every vehicle. For a company in the Republic of Moldova, the list should show which vehicle is used, by whom, where it travels and when each contract expires. RCA, CASCO and transport-related insurance serve different purposes.

This article is for a manager preparing renewal or taking over fleet administration. It focuses on inventories, records and proposal checks. It announces no universal discount and does not confirm acceptance of every use or vehicle category. Read the insurer's conditions for the actual fleet.

One shared working list for every vehicle

Start with a common record maintained by the responsible person. Include registration, vehicle identification number, category, manufacturing year, owner and user. Record the date checked. Two similarly named files with different versions can cause omissions even when each department believes it sent a complete list. Keep the date on the shared version visible so colleagues know which inventory was actually checked. Record later corrections against that version rather than silently replacing identifiers in a copy used for comparison.

Separate active vehicles from those sold, under repair or temporarily received. For leased vehicles, record ownership and contractual requirements to discuss. Do not mark protection confirmed merely because a vehicle appears in accounting records. Check each document's existence, period and precise vehicle identification.

Actual use matters when comparing proposals

A sales car, distribution van and truck do not have identical working patterns. Describe routes, frequency, parking locations and foreign use. Information should reflect ordinary operations, not only circumstances on the day a calculation was requested.

Declare taxi, courier, passenger transport or construction-site use separately where applicable. Do not assume acceptance under a proposal calculated for another activity. If use changes, ask what to communicate and how the response is recorded. A verbal reply does not replace applicable documents.

Keep RCA, CASCO, CMR and CARGO separate

Maintain separate entries for each vehicle's policies. RCA concerns motor third-party liability under applicable law and contract. CASCO is considered for the vehicle itself and risks accepted by the insurer. A CASCO policy does not replace RCA or confirm every possible damage scenario.

For transport, distinguish carrier liability from the interest in the goods. CMR and CARGO are not two names for identical protection. Ask about the subject, insured party, territory and events considered. A vehicle's presence in the fleet does not establish automatic inclusion of goods or company liability in the same policy.

The renewal calendar must be verifiable

Build the calendar from documents, not memories of the last payment. Record commencement, expiry and instalment dates where relevant. Establish who checks the list and approves expenditure. An alert sent to a former fleet administrator can leave renewal without a real owner even when the notification system works.

Prepare comparisons before expiry to allow clarification and inspections where requested. Do not assume automatic extension. Check the new documents and every vehicle's identification, not only the invoice. Sending an application, receiving a calculation or initiating payment is not the same as confirming protection is in force.

Read vehicle value and deductible together

For CASCO, prepare the value under consideration and its basis: purchase record, valuation or another justification requested by the provider. Ask which value is accepted and how it is used for any payment. A value in an internal spreadsheet does not become an insured sum simply because it was emailed.

The deductible is the share of a loss borne by the insured under the contract. Ask for its exact form, currency, percentage or amount and applicable situations. A lower premium may involve a different own contribution. Compare those elements for the same scenario, not only the annual total.

Questions about repairs and vehicle downtime

Before choosing, ask how damage is assessed, repairers selected and documents provided. Include warranty or leasing service requirements in the discussion. Do not assume every workshop, part or calculation method is accepted under every contract. Compare written answers to the same questions.

Separately assess downtime costs: delayed deliveries, temporary rental or reallocated routes. This is a budgeting exercise, not a statement that the policy pays those costs. If assistance or extra services are mentioned, check the provider, territory, limits and access procedure rather than inferring them from a package name.

Adding and removing vehicles

Establish an internal procedure for purchases, sales and replacements. Whoever receives a vehicle should notify policy administration as well as accounting. Ask the insurer how the list is amended and when changes take effect. Do not transfer one vehicle's document to another merely because the model or value matches.

When removing a vehicle, keep evidence of the change and the insurer's response. Any premium adjustment or termination must be checked individually. Do not promise standard refunds or delete the vehicle's history. A clear archive supports later explanations and avoids repeated requests for the same documents.

Claims history without unnecessary personal data

For renewal, prepare verifiable incident records: vehicle, date, type, status and supporting document. Separate open from settled files and estimates from confirmed payments. Do not present an internal estimate as paid compensation or omit unfinished cases to obtain an apparently better calculation.

Share only information needed for assessment through the agreed channel for sensitive records. Do not publish drivers' identity documents, personal numbers or full files through an open form. Prevention work can use aggregate themes such as parking impacts, windscreens, routes or busy periods. This does not replace accurate proposal information.

Compare proposals for the same fleet

Send the same inventory version and its date. Ask providers to identify accepted vehicles, those requiring information and exclusions from the list. Check period, territory, sums, exclusions and deductibles before the total premium. If vehicle lists differ, price alone cannot establish which option suits the company.

Use three labels: confirmed in documents, unclear and not included. Record the relevant page or endorsement beside each answer. Resolve discrepancies before signing. A general promise of complete protection does not explain foreign use, an additional driver or repairs undertaken before inspection.

A discount must be confirmed, not assumed

Vehicle numbers can matter commercially but do not establish an automatic discount. Request a calculation for the actual category, reference premium and conditions of any benefit. An up-to discount is a possible ceiling, not a guaranteed percentage for every vehicle, customer or policy.

Separate discounts from changes in protection. Where deductibles, territories or limits differ, do not describe the total difference as savings on an identical contract. Keep the comparison basis and internal approval. This article gives no fleet tariff and promises no benefit for RCA, CASCO, CMR or CARGO without checking the offer.

A practical file for the first discussion

Prepare the updated inventory, policy list, periods, uses and operational questions. Add relevant leasing or financing requirements. Do not begin by sending every driver's full archive. Agree the purpose first, then request the necessary documents and a secure transmission method.

Appoint one response coordinator and identify the department confirming each fact. Fleet management remains a company process; the broker can organise comparisons and explain options. The insurer decides acceptance and claims under the contract. Combining vehicles in one file does not change those responsibilities.

Handing administration to a new colleague

Hand over the current list, documents and unresolved questions. Check several entries together, such as a new vehicle, a leased one and an open claim if applicable. The aim is to find discrepancies, not certify the whole fleet from a sample. Assign responsibility for missing information.

Update notification recipients and people authorised to approve changes. Limit archive access to relevant roles without unnecessary driver-document distribution. Record the handover date and checked inventory version. The next administrator can then continue renewals and incident communication without reconstructing policies from old personal messages.

Frequently asked questions about fleet policy administration

Must every vehicle have identical protection?

No. Fleet membership does not establish this. Use, value and contractual requirements can differ. Request category-based assessment and check each vehicle's applicable documents.

Is a new vehicle automatically included?

Do not assume inclusion. Report the purchase and confirm the procedure, document and effective date. Retain the response before considering the update complete.

Does CMR insure the truck too?

Do not confuse carrier liability with vehicle insurance. Check CASCO, cargo and liability separately according to each contract's subject and conditions.

What is the first renewal step?

Confirm the inventory and expiry dates, then compare proposals for the same list version. Clarify use and gaps before choosing by price.
